subject: mathematics
question_text: If the points with position vectors 3i−2j−k, 2i+3j−4k, −i+j+2k and 4i+5j+λk are coplanar, then show that λ = −146/17.

mark_split.label: Set the scalar triple product to 0

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.58 — SAQ chapter 8 Addition of Vectors, answer 49.2. Printed appearances: AP 20 · TS 15,20. This is the coplanarity test run BACKWARDS — the same determinant, but set equal to zero and solved rather than evaluated, which is why it carries a solving step where the other four carry a concluding one. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed anywhere in this chapter. It follows the split the same book prints for the one 4-mark answer that does carry tags, Matrices answer 40 on book p.51. The book's chapter header carries ★★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q12 is the Addition of Vectors slot. NOTE: Addition of Vectors has NO Section-C slot on the paper and no LAQ chapter in this book — the unit is SAQ and VSAQ only.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find lambda here — say what is different from an ordinary coplanarity question.

steps.label: Write the position vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same opening as any coplanarity question — but note that λ rides along inside OS and must be carried as a letter all the way to the last line.
steps.memory_tip: Same opening as any coplanarity question, but λ rides inside OS and must be carried as a letter.

recall.must_convey: That the four given vectors are named as position vectors OP, OQ, OR, OS from an origin O, with λ kept as a letter inside OS.
accept: name the four position vectors OP OQ OR OS with lambda still inside OS
take the four points from the origin keeping lambda as a letter
write the position vectors, the last one has lambda in it
naalugu position vectors rasi, lambda ni letter ga unchali
let the given vectors be OP OQ OR and OS

steps.why: λ is unknown, so it cannot be evaluated — it has to survive every line until the equation that pins it down.
common_mistakes: Guessing a value for λ and checking it.

steps.label: Find PQ, PR and PS
steps.margin_note: Second mark. All three from P. Only PS carries λ, and it becomes (λ+1) because −(−1) = +1 — a sign slip here changes the final answer.
steps.memory_tip: Only PS carries λ, and it becomes (λ + 1) because −(−1) = +1. A sign slip here changes the answer.

recall.must_convey: That PQ, PR and PS are found by subtracting OP from the other three, and that the k component of PS becomes (λ+1).
accept: subtract OP from the other three, and PS gets lambda plus one in the k component
find the three edge vectors from P, the last one has lambda plus one
PS is i plus seven j plus lambda plus one k
OP ni teesi migatha moodu nunchi, PS lo lambda plus one vasthundi
the three vectors from P, one of them still carrying lambda

steps.why: Subtracting −k from λk gives λ + 1, not λ − 1. That single sign is the difference between −146/17 and a wrong answer.
common_mistakes: Writing (λ − 1)k by subtracting instead of adding.

steps.label: Set the determinant to 0
steps.margin_note: Third mark, and the whole idea. The points are GIVEN coplanar, so the scalar triple product is known to be zero — that known zero is the equation that determines λ.
steps.memory_tip: The points are GIVEN coplanar, so the triple product is known to be 0 — that is the equation for λ.
lines: The points are coplanar, so [PQ PR PS] = 0:

recall.must_convey: That being coplanar means the scalar triple product is ZERO, and that this is written as an equation in λ rather than evaluated.
accept: coplanar means the triple product is zero so set the determinant equal to zero
because they are coplanar the determinant is zero, that gives an equation in lambda
write the determinant and put it equal to zero
coplanar kabatti determinant zero, adi lambda equation isthundi
the scalar triple product must vanish, so equate it to zero

steps.why: Every other question in this chapter computes the determinant and finds it is zero. This one is told it is zero and works out what λ must be for that to happen.
common_mistakes: Evaluating the determinant without setting it to zero.
Trying to show it is zero for every λ, which it is not.

steps.label: Expand and solve
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Expand along the first row, collect the λ terms, and solve. The λ terms are −3λ and +20λ, which add to 17λ — the 17 in the answer comes from there.
steps.memory_tip: Collect the λ terms: −3λ + 20λ = 17λ, which is where the 17 in the answer comes from.

recall.must_convey: That the determinant is expanded, the λ terms collect to 17λ, and 17λ + 146 = 0 gives λ = −146/17.
accept: expand it, the lambda terms give seventeen lambda, so seventeen lambda plus one forty six equals zero and lambda is minus one forty six over seventeen
collecting lambda gives seventeen lambda plus one hundred forty six equals zero
solve to get lambda equals minus one forty six by seventeen
expand cheste seventeen lambda plus one forty six zero, lambda minus one forty six by seventeen
the answer is negative one hundred forty six over seventeen

steps.why: The two λ terms come from different parts of the expansion and have opposite signs, so they must be collected carefully — −3λ + 20λ is 17λ, not 23λ.
common_mistakes: Collecting the λ terms as 23λ by losing the minus.
Forgetting to distribute the −5 across both terms of its bracket.
Leaving the answer as 17λ = −146 without dividing.

insider_note: The unknown sits in PS alone, so build the other two rows numerically first. Setting the determinant to zero gives 17λ + 146 = 0; the answer is meant to be an awkward fraction.
